'''''Iris'' × ''hollandica''''', commonly known as the '''Dutch iris''', is a hybrid [[iris (plant)|iris]] developed from species native to Portugal, Spain and North Africa <ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Iridaceae/Iris_hollandica.html |title=Desert-Tropicals |access-date=23 June 2014 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304104723/http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Iridaceae/Iris_hollandica.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>  (''[[Iris tingitana]]'' × ''[[Iris xiphium]]'').<ref>{{cite web |title=Iris x hollandica |website=NCBI taxonomy database |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?lvl=0&id=35876}}</ref>

Two varieties of ''Iris xiphium'' (var. ''praecox'') from Spain and (var. ''lusitanica'') from Portugal, were crossed with ''Iris tingitana'' (from North Africa). This was carried out by a Dutch bulb firm 'Van Tubergen' (based in [[Haarlem]]) in the 19th century.<ref>Rina Kamenetsky and Hiroshi Okubo {{Google books|5B-ucdbgA3wC| Ornamental Geophytes: From Basic Science to Sustainable Production|page=83}}</ref>

Because the bulb could be forced in a greenhouse to flower early, it was popular with florists. Since the 1900s it has been crossed with other species to create various cultivars. After the Second World War, stocks of bulbs were imported to America. They then increased the color range mainly the yellows.<ref name="history" />

==Description==
''Iris'' × ''hollandica'' has a bulb of about {{convert|10|cm}} and can reach a height of about {{convert|60|cm}}. This [[bulb]]ous iris has narrow linear green leaves and bears largish blue to yellow to white flowers.<ref>[https://www.uniprot.org/taxonomy/35876 Iris hollandica], Uniprot</ref> They do not have any fragrance. They mainly bloom in May–June in the [[Northern Hemisphere]], and in September–October in the [[Southern Hemisphere]].

==Cultivars==
There are many known cultivars including;<ref name="history">{{cite web|first=D | last=Henry |year=2011|title=The Dutch Iris – A History Of Color| url=http://www.zone10.com/the-dutch-iris-a-history-of-color.html|website=zone10.com|access-date=1 August 2014}}</ref>

* 'Imperator' (dark blue)
* 'Wedgwood' (light blue)
* 'White Excelsior' (short white)
* 'Yellow Queen' (light yellow)
